The biggest Kestrel update yet: double-click to render, save straight to MP3, Opus or FLAC, and download a ready-made build instead of compiling one.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `kestrel-1.1.0-windows-x64.zip` | Windows 10/11 |
| `kestrel-1.1.0-macos-universal.dmg` | macOS 11 or newer (Apple silicon and Intel) |
| `kestrel-1.1.0-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 or newer) |

- **Windows:** unzip and double-click `kestrel.exe`. If SmartScreen warns you, click **More info → Run anyway**.
- **macOS:** copy `kestrel` out of the dmg. The first time you open it, allow it under **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**.
- **Linux:** extract it and run `./kestrel` in a terminal. You need a Vulkan driver.

The macOS and Linux builds haven't been tested yet. If you try one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/issues) and tell us how it went.

## Before you upgrade

- **The command line now needs `--force-cli`.** Running Kestrel with no arguments opens the new guided renderer.
- **`--volume` is now a percentage.** `100` is normal and `50` is half, so `--volume 0.5` becomes `--volume 50`.
- **Files that never set channel volume render 4.15 dB quieter**, which matches BASSMIDI.

## What's new

- **Guided renderer.** Double-click Kestrel, pick your MIDI, soundfonts, voices, format and folder, and watch the render progress.
- **Save to Opus, MP3, OGG, FLAC or M4A** by choosing the file extension. This needs ffmpeg, and `kestrel --force-cli get-ffmpeg` can download it for you.
- **SFZ LFOs play.** Tremolo (`amplfo_*`) and vibrato (`pitchlfo_*`) are now applied.
- **Closer to BASSMIDI.** Tempo changes and channel volume now behave the way BASSMIDI's do.
- **Huge files work.** Blocks with billions of notes no longer crash the render or run out of RAM.
- **Faster.** Renders take about 14% less time, and MIDI files with thousands of tracks load about 2.8× faster.
- **Less RAM at startup.** With a large piano library, the peak went from 2.6 GB to 1.1 GB.
- **An API for GUIs.** `kestrel --force-cli api` lets another program, such as a community GUI, drive Kestrel directly: load MIDIs and soundfonts, set any option, start and cancel renders, and get live stats (progress, notes, voices, speed, RAM and VRAM) instead of reading log text. See [API.md](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/blob/main/API.md).
- **VRAM use** now appears in the progress figures (Windows only).

## Fixes

- LFOs and modulation envelopes now start with their note, not up to 85 ms early.
- `--limiter omni` no longer clips.
- A wrong output extension is now an error, with a suggestion if it looks like a typo.
- Negative values such as `--ceiling-db -1` now work.
- A crash now shows a readable error instead of garbling the progress screen.

## Known issues

- Kestrel is louder than BASSMIDI. To match it, use `--volume 78`, or `--volume 55` for stereo SFZ soundfonts.
- Presets with no attack or release can click at the start and end of notes.
- On some soundfonts, notes can keep sounding after the music stops.
- On the densest files, the CPU is the bottleneck.
- General MIDI support is still basic.
